name: abort-keeps-executed-steps
note: stopped is only reachable through a stop signal, so the fixture declares its own driver: abortAfterSteps 1 aborts on the step announced after the first one, i.e. once the first tap has already been applied to the device. Replayed with no driver the script runs on — the model client clamps past the end of the script and repeats tap(3,4) — until the loop guard stops it with 5 steps, which is not the scenario this fixture describes. No retry budget is involved here: the first step scripts ok, and an unscripted device call also resolves ok.
